title: Cell Cycle Overview & G0 Phase
keyTakeaways: Sequence of events: G1 → S → G2 → M phase.
Interphase accounts for >95% of total cycle duration; M phase takes <5%.
G0 (quiescent phase): cells withdraw from cycling yet maintain cellular metabolism.
examAlert: G0 cells remain metabolically active, not dead or inactive.
quickReviseSummary: The cycle coordinates replication and division. Differentiated non-cycling cells rest in metabolically active G0.

title: S Phase (Synthesis Phase)
keyTakeaways: Nuclear DNA replicates: content doubles from 2C to 4C.
Centrosome (centriole pair) duplicates in the cytoplasm simultaneously.
examAlert: Amount of DNA doubles (2C → 4C), but chromosome number does NOT double.
quickReviseSummary: S phase duplicates DNA (2C to 4C) and cytoplasmic centrioles while conserving chromosome ploidy (2n).

title: Metaphase Mechanics
keyTakeaways: Chromosomes attain maximal condensation; best stage for morphological study.
Spindle fibers attach to protein kinetochores on sister chromatids.
Chromosomes line up along equatorial metaphase plate.
examAlert: Metaphase is the benchmark stage to analyze chromosome count, shape, and structure.
quickReviseSummary: Maximal compaction, equatorial alignment at the metaphase plate, and dual kinetochore spindle docking.

title: Anaphase Segregation
keyTakeaways: Sister chromatids separate into daughter chromosomes.
Centromeres lead toward poles while chromosome arms trail.
examAlert: Centromere cleavage marks the transition from metaphase to anaphase.
quickReviseSummary: Centromeres split concurrently, and daughter chromosomes diverge to opposing poles with arms trailing behind.

title: Pachytene & Genetic Recombination
keyTakeaways: Substage of Prophase I following zygotene synapsis.
Recombination nodules form between non-sister chromatids.
Recombinase-catalyzed crossing over produces new genetic combinations.
examAlert: Recombination involves non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes and requires the enzyme recombinase.
quickReviseSummary: Non-sister chromatids of homologous bivalents exchange genetic segments via recombinase, generating diversity.
